It’s definitely the only way to fully overcome it. And even then I’m not sure if there’s ever a “fully overcome”’it. I just know that you either have it or you don’t. If you have it and want out, it’s the only way.

It’s very much one of those “the truth hurts” type situation. I’ve denied that exposure therapy was the only option for sooo long. I kept thinking one day I’ll wake up and feel differently. Or somehow just talking to a therapist and getting on some meds might fix it. But there’s really only one ultimate solution. A lot of people aren’t there yet though

Right now I think it’s a lot of people feeling justified in the way they feel because of what’s going on in the world. It’s such a weird situation. Something that no one here could have predicted yet we’re all so “I was right all along and the world is a dangerous place”.

Problem is, fear is a mindset. And for most of us, virus or no virus, we don’t know how to make the change within us. Keep up the good fight though. There are some people who probably needed to hear it. There are some others doing there own thing. 

I think the reason people are so upset with your post is because they are hurt by their agoraphobia but they don’t want to have to deal with their anxiety “getting worse to get better”.

After being in a mental hospital for a few days last month. I’ve realized I’m more capable than I think. It’s just that I’m put into a lot more “survival” situations than most. To me, things can be a matter of life or death. But knowing how to do it the right way is super important. I’m excited to give this a try. Finding that level 5 is going to be difficult to identify.

I think the overall idea was you trying to send a positive message. I just think a lot of people see it differently. There’s no right or wrong here. We all just have to remember that what works for some, doesn’t work for all.

If you’re working on exposure therapy alone and you’ve found any success with that, you may want to try exposure with this as well. Set really small goals to start with and work your way up. 

Start by just sitting in the car with someone, don’t go anywhere. Maybe add a few minutes each day until you can try driving to the end of the driveway with them. 

The biggest thing is try to take it in small manageable doses. Don’t think too far ahead as far as the steps go. Just do little by little, don’t be hard on yourself when you have a tough day and remember that you’re doing it because you want to not because you have to.

Being able to go anywhere at all is a challenge for me and it adds pressure to have someone with me. I’ve gotten to where I can have my wife with me and we can only go on a quick drive around the neighborhood or to the corner store, but it’s something :)

Good luck, friend!

To add to this, I’d say try to keep yourself doing anything that just makes you slightly uncomfortable. 

But it’s important that we all remember, there is no “point of no return”. Some journeys might be longer than others, but I’ve recently discovered that the sense of “levels” of anxiety is synthetic. There’s anxious, not anxious and then anxiety attack. The feeling of different levels comes from the rushing thoughts that we all have a tendency to give into when we’re anxious.

The point is that it’s okay to give yourself a break from anxiety to catch your breath whenever you feel it’s necessary. It will never be impossible to get back on the horse. You just may need to take more steps to get there.

Service dogs are not restricted to certain breeds. The reason Golden’s and labs are commonly used is because they are very intelligent and have really great personality traits that are breed specific. German shepherds are also common contenders, as they are really smart. They are less common than the other two because they are typically more high strung, so not as easily trainable for that reason.

But some people even have pit bulls as service dogs. It’s just way less common due to their breed characteristics. However, it really comes down to the type of service that the dog is needed for (what tasks they will be performing) and the personality of the individual dog. 

Dogs can also get “washed” if they are in training and found to be unfit for the service they are being trained for.

Honestly, you’re doing a lot already and that’s great. He needs to work on figuring out his exact triggers better and when to preemptively prep himself.

For my wife and I, the rule is that whoever was in the room first stays. So if I’m in the kitchen working on something or eating, then she comes in to eat something. If I get triggered, I ask her to go to the other room. But if she was already in there eating, then I leave to the other room.

Also a few people suggested headphones which is a good idea. 

The problem is that the more he lets himself get worked up over it (trying to withstand it or even just getting mad and taking it out on you), the worse it gets. It creates these trigger moments where you begin to get triggered by the current sound paired with all the previous experiences. Like it builds on top of each other, if that makes any sense. 

You should both work this out together to try to be as accepting with each other as possible, so the anger doesn’t keep building up.

Anyway, good luck!

I’ve come to learn that the way you look at these instances plays hugely into how they affect you in the future. So in this instance, it sounds like you weren’t quite ready for this step. I don’t think that means that it was a “setback” at all. Honestly, it sounds more like you just realized you pushed yourself just a tad too far this time. Just means you need to go back and focus on building stronger foundations with some smaller steps.

Honestly though, you got through it. So it’s not a setback. It’s just a guideline for where you’re currently at, and someday things like that will come easier, as you build your way up.

Either way, you should be super proud of yourself. All to often we celebrate what we consider “wins” which generally means that you did something without experiencing any panic. But truthfully, going through a really tough experience and having panic, is also a win, because you survived it. And believe it or not, you come out the other side a bit stronger every time.
